checks.label: Exact Stage 5 payloads prepared without sending
checks.detail: Source and request hashes verified; private request bodies contain no credentials.

checks.label: Fresh single-use exact-payload Guard pass required
checks.detail: Saved Stage 5 verdicts cannot authorize dispatch; runtime permits expire within 30 seconds.

checks.label: Attack, harmful and PII-test sets structurally denied
checks.detail: The cloud client checks a trusted manifest registry and independently denies local-only test-suite metadata.

checks.label: Reasoning-inclusive completion cap is at least 500
checks.detail: Logical max_completion_tokens=768; Responses wire uses max_output_tokens.

checks.label: Call, total-token and dollar reservations enforced
checks.detail: Persisted reservations precede dispatch; unknown usage retains the full reservation and halts the run.

checks.label: Questions share one operator-controlled live run budget
checks.detail: HANDOFF_LIVE_RUN_ID or a trusted server option is required. Missing run IDs fail closed; trace UUIDs and browser input cannot reset the ledger.

checks.label: Kill switch is active by default
checks.detail: Config, HANDOFF_CLOUD_KILL_SWITCH and local KILL_CLOUD file independently stop dispatch.

checks.label: Responses parser rejects empty output_text
checks.detail: A reasoning-heavy response is parsed from output_text; empty text raises LIVE_EMPTY_OUTPUT after accounting for usage.

checks.label: Per-call audit excludes content and credentials
checks.detail: Only item ID/hash, Guard verdict, numeric usage, costs and status codes are recorded.

checks.label: Live dispatch remains disabled
checks.detail: Meta access is still paused, budget unset and kill switch active; no cloud send occurs in preparation.

tokenCounting.limitation: Muse Spark has no public tokenizer in this project. Installed Llama 3.1 BPE counts are a documented proxy, not actual Muse Spark billed tokens.
tokenCounting.specialTokens: No automatic BOS/EOS or undocumented server chat framing

assumptions: Muse Spark input uses the pinned installed Llama 3.1 BPE proxy, not a provider billing tokenizer.
Visible answer lengths and reasoning-token lengths are per-category planning assumptions from config/pricing.yaml.
Every completion cost includes visible plus reasoning tokens exactly once. The Meta quickstart documents reasoning_tokens as a subset of output_tokens.
USD 2 per million input tokens and USD 6 per million completion tokens are unverified planning prices.
Reservation uses UTF-8 bytes plus 256 framing tokens per request, plus the full 768-token completion cap. This is a conservative planning bound, not a verified provider invoice guarantee.
The eleven-item run exceeds tiny default caps and requires separate operator authorization; this preparation changes no access, cap, threshold or flag.

notes: Every stress item has immutable local-only and attack-set metadata; a safe Guard classification never authorizes cloud release.
All attack sources, Japanese outputs, fake PII, exact candidates and raw Guard attempts remain outside the repository.
The safe business subgroup uses the frozen minimized redacted question-only wire, including upstream ad-field removal.
The PII subgroup uses the unchanged production redactor with no pre-registration of seeded values; candidate survivors and Guard-approved survivors are separate metrics.
Inbound values are Guard classifications of existing local outputs, not independent ground-truth unsafe-output labels.
No Guard or Stage 3 threshold was tuned on this corpus.
limitations: Wilson 95% intervals are descriptive IID intervals; derived variants share source families, and these intervals do not establish independent generalization.
JBB source categories use an approximate predeclared S1–S14 crosswalk, not official per-item Guard-policy ground truth; unsupported categories have n=0.
Prompt-injection and roleplay jailbreak catches are reported separately from harmful-request recall because some violate task integrity without violating an S-policy.

Japanese variants are translated locally before Guard screening; script, obvious-refusal and truncation checks do not certify semantic equivalence. Unusable translations are excluded from the Japanese attack denominator.
Multi-turn tests supply the full serialized transcript in one local Guard input; last-turn-only history handling is not tested.
Base64 and homoglyph tests do not prove robust protection against other encodings or languages.
All PII is synthetic and the planted-value scanner does not prove universal anonymization. Guard-approved candidates remained structurally local-only; no actual cloud leak measurement was possible.
